properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued November 22 at 1:28AM CST by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
At 128 AM CST, trained weather spotters reported a strong
thunderstorm 9 miles east of Hinton, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Trained weather spotters reported a 50 mph wind gust in
Hinton.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
El Reno, Yukon, Hinton, Union City, Okarche, Calumet, Bridgeport,
Cogar, Concho, Cedar Lake, and Richland.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued November 22 at 1:19AM CST by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
At 119 AM CST, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 3 miles west of Norge to 6 miles east of Rush
Springs to near Marlow. Movement was northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Chickasha, Marlow, Lindsay, Rush Springs, Bray, Alex, Bradley,
Agawam, Tabler, Central High, Ninnekah, Acme, and Cox City.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 22 at 3:15AM AST until November 22 at 5:15AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Humacao in Puerto Rico...
Maunabo in Puerto Rico...
Yabucoa in Puerto Rico...

* WHEN...Until 515 AM AST.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Water over
roadways. River or stream flows are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 315 AM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
properties.area: Humacao, PR; Maunabo, PR; Yabucoa, PR

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:36PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb through Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
reach Major Flood Stage late this weekend. A steady rise through
Major Flood Stage is anticipated through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 5.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 5.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise into Major Flood Stage
early next week, reaching 6.0 feet mid week. Additional rises are
possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has allowed the St Johns River at Sanford to continue
rising through Moderate Flood Stage, Additional rises are anticipated
through next week, reaching Major Flood Stage by the middle of next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding becomes more significant to low
lying structures and marinas along the river in Volusia and
Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 7.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 7.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue a steady rise,
reaching 8.2 feet late next week. Additional rises are possible
thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:27PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. Continued
rises through Major Flood Stage are forecast through this weekend.
River levels may begin to slowly decline next week while remaining in
Major Flood Stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 12.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 12.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.0 feet
this weekend, with a slow and steady decline forecast thereafter.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:23PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to reach Major Flood Stage, well above
its previous record flood stage. The river level will remain steady
into the middle of next week, with a chance for the start of a slow
decline late next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Saturday the stage was 18.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Saturday was 18.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage at 18.8 feet through this weekend and into early next
week. The start of a slow decline may be possible late next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:21PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused river
levels on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage.
Continued rises through Major Flood Stage are forecast through next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 4.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to gradually rise through Major
Flood Stage, reaching 4.3 feet into the middle of next week.
Additional rises thereafter will be possible.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 3:20PM MST until November 27 at 3:15PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 313 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
